source_title: Soar with Dragonfly: Send Your Name to Saturn’s moon Titan
source_excerpt:
Dragonfly, the first-of-its-kind rotorcraft to explore another world, will fly to various locations on Saturn’s moon Titan and investigate the moon’s habitability.
As NASA launches its Dragonfly rotorcraft toward one of the most extraordinary destinations in the solar system, Saturn’s moon Titan, you can join the mission. Sign up today to have your name placed on a chip aboard Dragonfly and get your personalized boarding pass for this daring exploration adventure. Las tarjetas de embarque también están disponibles en español.
Dragonfly isn’t a mission to detect life — it’s a mission to investigate the chemistry that came before biology here on Earth.
Dragonfly Principal Investigator, Planetary Scientist at Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory
An Airborne Science Mission Like No Other Never before have humans planned an airborne science mission to another world like Dragonfly. The Dragonfly rotorcraft will break the barriers for exploration of other planetary bodies. Instead of being limited to just the region around its landing site, Dragonfly’s rotors will carry it for miles across Titan during its planned 3.3-year mission, stopping to explore a variety of geologically interesting areas along the way, including dunes and Selk Crater. Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every 1-2 Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days. Artist's concept of Dragonfly on the surface of Titan NASA/Johns Hopkins APL

Instead of being limited to just the region around its landing site, Dragonfly’s rotors will carry it for miles across Titan during its planned 3.3-year mission, stopping to explore a variety of geologically interesting areas along the way, including dunes and Selk Crater. Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every 1-2 Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days.
Sampling the Surface Traveling several miles on each flight through the yellowish, smoggy haze of Titan’s nitrogen-rich atmosphere, Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments. The exploration of these diverse locations will help to characterize the habitability of Titan’s environment, investigate how far prebiotic chemistry has progressed, identify compounds of astrobiological interest, and even search for chemical indicators of water-based or hydrocarbon-based life. Artist's concept of Dragonfly lifting off from the surface of Titan. NASA/Johns Hopkins APL

NASA and Johns Hopkins APL give viewers an inside look at NASA's Dragonfly mission as it reaches another exciting milestone on the path to Saturn's moon Titan. Hear directly from Dragonfly scientists and engineers as they discuss the spacecraft's latest progress through integration and testing, explain how Dragonfly will explore Titan, and answer audience questions about the mission.
You may never soar under the clouds or over the organic sands of Saturn’s moon Titan, but your name can.…
Separated from its protective backshell, NASA’s Dragonfly rotorcraft autonomously speeds over the sand dunes of Titan. It scans the terrain…
Peeking into the clean room at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, it might be one…
New Frontiers Dragonfly was selected in 2019 as the fourth mission of NASA’s New Frontiers program, which conducts planetary science investigations using innovative and efficient approaches to answering unique science questions throughout our solar system. New Frontiers is managed for NASA's Science Mission Directorate in Washington by the Planetary Missions Program Office at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama. Mission Team Dragonfly is being designed and built under the direction of the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, which manages the mission for NASA. Elizabeth (Zibi) Turtle of APL is the principal investigator. The Dragonfly team includes key partners at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland; Lockheed Martin Space in Littleton, Colorado; NASA’s Ames Research Center in California’s Silicon Valley; NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia; Penn State University in State College, Pennsylvania; Malin Space Science Systems in San Diego; Honeybee Robotics in Pasadena, California; NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California; CNES (Centre National d’Etudes Spatiales) in Paris; the German Aerospace Center (DLR) in Cologne, Germany; and JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) in Tokyo. hi_body:
नासा अंतरिक्ष प्रेमियों को अपने आगामी ड्रैगूनफ्लाई मिशन में भाग लेने का अवसर दे रहा है, जिसके तहत वे अंतरिक्ष यान पर जाने वाली एक माइक्रोचिप में शामिल करने के लिए अपना नाम भेज सकते हैं।

ड्रैगूनफ्लाई एक नियोजित एयरबोर्न विज्ञान मिशन है जिसे शनि के चंद्रमा टाइटन का पता लगाने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। वर्ष 2019 में नासा के न्यू फ्रंटियर्स कार्यक्रम के चौथे मिशन के रूप में चयनित इस अंतरिक्ष यान को जीवन का प्रत्यक्ष पता लगाने के बजाय टाइटन की रहने योग्य स्थितियों और प्रीबायोटिक रसायन विज्ञान की जांच के लिए विकसित किया जा रहा है।

## मिशन का अवलोकन और उद्देश्य

* **गंतव्य:** शनि का चंद्रमा टाइटन, जो नाइट्रोजन-समृद्ध वातावरण और कार्बनिक रेत के टीलों से युक्त है।
* **डिज़ाइन:** अपनी तरह का पहला रोटरक्राफ्ट जो 3.3 साल के नियोजित मिशन के दौरान भूभाग पर मीलों की दूरी तय करने में सक्षम है।
* **संचालन:** इसके हर 1 से 2 टाइटन दिवस (जिसे ट्सोल कहा जाता है और जो लगभग 16 पृथ्वी दिवसों के बराबर होता है) पर एक उड़ान भरने की उम्मीद है, इस दौरान यह सेल्क क्रेटर जैसे विभिन्न भूवैज्ञानिक स्थलों पर सतह के नमूनों का अध्ययन करेगा।

## नेतृत्व और सहयोग

इस मिशन का प्रबंधन लॉरेल, मैरीलैंड में स्थित जॉन्स हॉपकिन्स एप्लाइड फिजिक्स लेबोरेटरी (APL) द्वारा मुख्य अन्वेषक एलिजाबेथ (ज़िबी) टर्टल के निर्देशन में किया जा रहा है। सहयोगी संस्थानों में नासा के कई केंद्र, सीएनएसएस (CNES), डीएलआर (DLR) और जैक्सा (JAXA) जैसी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अंतरिक्ष एजेंसियां, तथा अकादमिक और औद्योगिक भागीदार शामिल हैं।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ और सत्यापन

प्रतिभागी व्यक्तिगत बोर्डिंग पास प्राप्त करने के लिए आधिकारिक नासा चैनलों के माध्यम से साइन अप कर सकते हैं। मिशन के अपडेट की पुष्टि करने, तकनीकी विनिर्देशों की समीक्षा करने या सार्वजनिक भागीदारी विवरण की जांच करने के लिए, इच्छुक व्यक्तियों को नासा की आधिकारिक मिशन वेबसाइट और जॉन्स हॉपकिन्स एप्लाइड फिजिक्स लेबोरेटरी की घोषणाओं का संदर्भ लेना चाहिए।

en_body:
NASA is offering space enthusiasts an opportunity to participate in its upcoming Dragonfly mission by submitting their names to be included on a microchip aboard the rotorcraft. 

Dragonfly is a planned airborne science mission designed to explore Saturn’s moon Titan. Selected in 2019 as the fourth mission in NASA’s New Frontiers program, the spacecraft is being developed to investigate Titan's habitability and prebiotic chemistry rather than actively detect living organisms.

## Mission Overview and Objectives

* **Destination:** Saturn’s moon Titan, characterized by a nitrogen-rich atmosphere and organic sand dunes.
* **Design:** A first-of-its-kind rotorcraft capable of flying miles across the terrain during a planned 3.3-year mission.
* **Operations:** Expected to execute one flight every 1 to 2 Titan days (known as a Tsol, lasting roughly 16 Earth days), stopping to sample surface materials at sites like Selk Crater.

## Leadership and Collaboration

The mission is managed by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland, under the direction of Principal Investigator Elizabeth (Zibi) Turtle. Collaborating institutions include multiple NASA centers, international space agencies such as CNES, DLR, and JAXA, as well as academic and industrial partners.

## Practical Implications and Verification

Participants can sign up via official NASA channels to receive a personalized boarding pass. To verify mission updates, review technical specifications, or check public participation details, interested individuals should consult NASA's official mission website and announcements from Johns Hopkins APL.
